body.statement: Open-ended Question 1. Can the rational-chart handle \(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal I}\) be constructed so that, for every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\) and every \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\), some retained chart has a nonzero pullback of \(F_{D,y}\) on a rational open box realizing the exact oracle, with a chart count and grid denominator bounded by \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\); and can the bound be reduced to singly exponential when every minimum DAG has bounded treewidth?
body.justification: This exposes the constructive graph-native content required to prove Theorem 1 without appealing to an unjustified density of rational points on arbitrary CI varieties.
body.gap: Directed-forest CI ideals have tractable prime parameterizations, but no existing atlas is known to be effect-separating for all signatures induced by tied sparsest DAGs.
body.consumer: A positive answer yields finite rational witness search and practical certificate bounds; a negative answer identifies the precise family on which SparseSIM-ID must return algebraic rather than rational witnesses.
